decisions.evidence: Entry 5 (maker): “paste the link, then press Save”; Entry 6 (client): “Pasting a link and pressing Save is the quick capture I had in mind.”
decisions.note: Conforming URL-save decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 (maker): “automatically make a short readable label from the link”; Entry 6 (client): “isn’t enough… collect the page’s real title and short description, along with its site icon and preview image.”
decisions.note: The initial generated-label behavior replaced required remote metadata collection; corrected during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 (maker) offers only URL capture and asks whether a title or note is needed; Entry 6 (client): “correct the title or description before saving and edit them afterward.”
decisions.note: The client supplied missing pre-save and post-save metadata editing requirements.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 (maker): each item shows an auto-label and full address; Entry 6 (client) asks for real title, description, site icon, and preview image.
decisions.note: The initial card presentation omitted required readability context such as description and favicon.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 (maker) defines cards with only a label and address; Entry 6 (client) requests metadata but does not mention visible tags. The omission is surfaced only after the revised presentation in Entries 7–8.
decisions.note: Visible tags were still missing from the first list-item decision and passed without expression at that stage.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 (maker) presents saving without duplicate handling; Entry 6 (client): “saving the same address again shouldn’t add a duplicate… take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it.”
decisions.note: Duplicate convergence was missing from the initial save flow and was requested during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 (maker) presents fetched title, description, icon, preview, a review panel, and later editing; Entry 8 (client) accepts the review step and later title/description editing.
decisions.note: Revised metadata-fetch and editing behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 (maker) defines cards with thumbnail, title, icon, description, and address but no tags; Entry 8 (client): “When organising is added, I’d expect each item’s tags to be visible here too.”
decisions.note: The revised card still omitted the required visible tags; the client explicitly required their later inclusion.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 (maker): duplicates ignore protocol, `www`, capitalization, and trailing slash; Entry 8 (client): paths and queries must retain case and `http`/`https` and `www` variants must not automatically be conflated.
decisions.note: The proposed equivalence rule could merge distinct URLs; the client supplied a safer same-URL rule.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 (maker) presents later editing of title and description; Entry 8 (client): “I’ll also need to be able to correct the saved address itself from that editor.”
decisions.note: URL editing was missing from the presented editor.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 (maker) says `https://SITE.com/Article?ref=A/` should duplicate `…?ref=A`; Entry 10 (client) explains the slash is inside the query and supplies `https://SITE.com/Article/?ref=A` as the harmless-path-slash case.
decisions.note: The duplicate test incorrectly normalized query data; the client corrected the rule.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 (maker) allows changing the address; Entry 10 (client): “reject text that isn’t a valid web link rather than saving any non-empty text.”
decisions.note: The URL editor lacked validation that the saved value was a web URL.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 (maker) presents query-safe duplicate matching and rejects non-HTTP(S) editor values; Entry 12 (client): “those cases now behave as I expect.”
decisions.note: The corrected URL editing and duplicate-convergence decisions conform.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13 (maker): search covers title, description, and web address; Entry 14 (client): “Once bookmarks can have notes, those need to be searched too.”
decisions.note: The initial full-text search scope omitted notes.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13 (maker) presents search behavior without a case rule; Entry 14 (client): “it should ignore capitalisation.”
decisions.note: Case-insensitive matching was supplied as a missing search requirement.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13 (maker) supports only implicit all-word matching; Entry 14 (client) requests `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, parentheses, and quoted operator words.
decisions.note: Boolean operators, grouping, negation, and literal quoted operators were missing from the presented query behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13 (maker) presents ordinary word search; Entry 14 (client) requests “an exact quoted phrase.”
decisions.note: Exact phrase search was missing from the initial search presentation.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13 (maker) searches ordinary bookmark text; Entry 14 (client): “typing `#tagname` should search by tag rather than merely finding those characters in the text.”
decisions.note: Tag-aware search syntax was missing and explicitly requested.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 (maker) presents case-insensitive matching, exact phrases, Boolean operators, parentheses, and quoted literals; Entry 16 (client): “the query behaviour matches what I expect.”
decisions.note: The revised query-language behavior conforms; deferred note and tag support are evaluated at their later presentations.

decisions.evidence: Entry 17 (maker) presents unread/read toggling and separate To read filtering; Entry 18 (client) accepts the filters, counts, and manual per-item toggle.
decisions.note: The presented read-later state, unread view, and mark-as-read behavior conform.

decisions.evidence: Entry 19 (maker): ordinary saved references are “slightly dimmed”; Entry 20 (client): “should look just as prominent as other bookmarks in the All view.”
decisions.note: Dimming deliberately retained reference bookmarks undermined the readability-first list; the client requested equal prominence.

decisions.evidence: Entry 21 (maker) presents opt-in Read later, equal visual prominence, a To read label, and reversible state actions; Entry 22 (client): “I’m happy with this flow.”
decisions.note: The revised read-later presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 23 (maker) supports multiple tags during save/edit, displays tag chips, click-to-filter, and `#tag` search; Entry 24 (client) accepts those behaviors.
decisions.note: Core tag assignment, visibility, editing, filtering, and search syntax conform.

decisions.evidence: Entry 23 (maker) presents free tag entry; Entry 24 (client): “as I type, the field should suggest matching tags I’ve already used.”
decisions.note: Existing-tag autocomplete was missing from tag entry.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25 (maker) presents matching existing-tag suggestions with keyboard or click selection; Entry 26 (client): “That suggestion behaviour feels right.”
decisions.note: The revised tag autocomplete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 27 (maker) asks whether search/tag filters and simple scrolling are sufficient for a large collection; Entry 28 (client): “I’d want to sort at least by date added and title.”
decisions.note: The proposed large-list behavior omitted sorting.

decisions.evidence: Entry 29 (maker) presents newest, oldest, title A–Z, and title Z–A sorting; Entry 30 (client): “The sort dropdown is clear.”
decisions.note: The implemented list sorting conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 29 (maker) fixes Newest first as the default; Entry 30 (client): “I should be able to choose my default sort order… and have those choices remembered.”
decisions.note: Remembered personal default-sort configuration was missing.

decisions.evidence: Entry 29 (maker) fixes chunks at 20 items; Entry 30 (client) requests choosing “20, 50, or 100” and remembering the choice.
decisions.note: The displayed-items preference was presented as a fixed value rather than a personal setting.

decisions.evidence: Entry 29 (maker) proposes locking the large-list display behavior without text-size controls; Entry 30 (client): “I’d also like a simple text-size setting.”
decisions.note: The display settings omitted font-size adjustment.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31 (maker) presents remembered default sort, items-per-load, and text-size settings; Entry 32 (client): “The settings themselves feel right.”
decisions.note: The personal display-setting behavior conforms. Cross-device persistence was a deployment expectation beyond this functional item.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31 (maker) says the whole goal is covered and proposes scope lock; Entry 32 (client) refuses because “deleting links” has not been explored.
decisions.note: Permanent bookmark deletion was absent at the attempted specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31 (maker) proposes locking scope; Entry 32 (client) requests “putting links aside in a reversible archive.”
decisions.note: Archive, archive/delete distinction, and the archive view were missing at the attempted specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31 (maker) proposes locking scope; Entry 32 (client) identifies “adding notes” as an unexplored manage behavior.
decisions.note: Bookmark notes were missing at the attempted specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31 (maker) proposes locking scope; Entry 32 (client) requests “changing many selected links at once.”
decisions.note: Multi-selection and filtered-collection bulk actions were absent at the attempted specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31 (maker) proposes locking scope; Entry 32 (client) requests “saving useful search-and-tag combinations.”
decisions.note: Saved dynamic filters/bundles were absent at the attempted specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31 (maker) proposes locking scope; Entry 32 (client) requests “keeping a preserved copy of a page.”
decisions.note: Local snapshots were absent at the attempted specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31 (maker) proposes locking scope without external preservation; the preservation exploration requested in Entry 32 leads to the explicit Internet Archive requirement in Entry 48.
decisions.note: Internet Archive preservation was missing from the proposed scope; the linked preservation discussion supplied it before scope lock.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31 (maker) proposes locking scope; Entry 32 (client) requests importing bookmarks.
decisions.note: Netscape/browser bookmark import was absent at the attempted specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31 (maker) proposes locking scope; Entry 32 (client) requests exporting bookmarks.
decisions.note: Netscape/browser bookmark export was absent at the attempted specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33 (maker) presents reversible archive, an Archived view, restore, permanent confirmed deletion, and exclusion from ordinary lists/search; Entry 34 (client): “exactly what I want.”
decisions.note: The archive/delete behavior conforms. Menu placement feedback is orthogonal to the reference requirements.

decisions.evidence: Entry 35 (maker): “Search finds notes”; Entry 36 (client): “searching it alongside the other bookmark text is exactly what I want.”
decisions.note: Full-text search was extended to notes as required.

decisions.evidence: Entry 35 (maker) presents plain note entry and a trimmed card preview; Entry 36 (client) requests a full view and “simple Markdown… display that formatting when I view the note.”
decisions.note: The initial notes flow lacked Markdown rendering and a non-editing full-note view.

decisions.evidence: Entry 37 (maker) supports headings, emphasis, links, and lists but excludes “Images, tables, and code blocks”; Entry 38 (client): “I don’t need images, tables, or code blocks here.”
decisions.note: At prototype review, the client explicitly accepted a limited Markdown subset rather than broader Markdown rendering.

decisions.evidence: Entry 39 (maker) offers bulk reading state, archive/restore, add tag, and delete but says tag action “only adds”; Entry 40 (client): “I do need both bulk Add tag and Remove tag.”
decisions.note: Bulk remove-tag was missing from the presented bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Entry 39 (maker) presents explicit multi-selection and Select all over the complete filtered set; Entry 40 (client) confirms whole-current-filter selection is “exactly right.”
decisions.note: Selection and whole-filter bulk scope conform; remove-tag is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Entry 41 (maker) adds Remove tag while preserving unrelated tags; Entry 42 (client): “bulk tag removal now behaves correctly.”
decisions.note: The revised bulk tag actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Entry 43 (maker) saves a named search, tag expressions, list filter, and sort and recomputes matches dynamically; Entry 44 (client) accepts live recomputation and restoration but prefers explicit tag pickers.
decisions.note: Encoding included/excluded tags through `#tag` and `NOT #tag` is functionally equivalent to bundle conditions; the picker request is a UI preference, not a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: Entry 45 (maker) presents explicit included/excluded tag pickers, search, filter, sort, and dynamic matching; Entry 46 (client): “saved views now behave as I want.”
decisions.note: The revised saved-view presentation also conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 47 (maker) says the prototype copy body is simulated from metadata and only describes preserved content generally; Entry 48 (client): “should be a self-contained page that still opens if the original site disappears.”
decisions.note: The presented preservation flow did not yet specify the required single-file local HTML snapshot.

decisions.evidence: Entry 47 (maker) presents one page-copy behavior without a PDF rule; Entry 48 (client): “If the original address is a PDF, save the PDF itself.”
decisions.note: PDF-specific preservation was missing.

decisions.evidence: Entry 47 (maker) presents only a local copy; Entry 48 (client): “Give me an option to preserve the page through the Internet Archive as well.”
decisions.note: Internet Archive preservation was missing from the page-preservation presentation.

decisions.evidence: Entry 49 (maker) detects a PDF when the URL ends in `.pdf`; Entry 50 (client): “recognise the file it receives… whenever it actually is one.”
decisions.note: Suffix-only PDF detection could mishandle extensionless PDF responses; the client supplied content-based detection.

decisions.evidence: Entry 49 (maker) presents separate optional Internet Archive preservation and a link to the archived version; Entry 50 (client): “Those two preservation options are the right split.”
decisions.note: Internet Archive preservation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 51 (maker) says HTML import “creates bookmarks from its links” without promising metadata preservation; Entry 52 (client): “HTML import… should preserve each bookmark’s title, tags, and original date added.”
decisions.note: The browser-bookmark import presentation omitted required title, tag, and date preservation.

decisions.evidence: Entry 51 (maker) exports browser-standard HTML with title, address, date, and tags; Entry 52 (client) accepts the standard HTML format and flat tagged list.
decisions.note: Netscape/browser HTML export conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 51 (maker) says import merges and skips duplicates using the same URL rule; Entry 52 (client): “Merge-and-skip is the right default.”
decisions.note: Duplicate convergence during import conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 53 (maker) presents the “whole scope” without stating list-item navigation; Entry 54 (client): “selecting a bookmark opens its original address” must remain explicit.
decisions.note: Original-URL navigation was omitted at the final specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 53 (maker) summarizes only reversible Archive; Entry 54 (client) requires archived bookmarks to stay out of normal lists/searches while remaining searchable and restorable in Archived.
decisions.note: The final scope summary omitted the archive visibility and dedicated-view rules, which the client restored before lock.

decisions.evidence: Entry 55 (maker): “page copies store extracted readable text”; Entry 56 (client): “not the self-contained saved page we agreed on… a single local HTML file.”
decisions.note: The delivered implementation contradicted the required snapshot format and was rejected during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Entry 57 (maker) says normal captures are complete HTML with styles/images inlined and PDFs remain actual PDFs; Entry 58 (client): “updated page capture now produces the self-contained HTML we agreed on.”
decisions.note: The corrected snapshot implementation conforms.

decision.evidence: Entry 51 (maker) calls JSON a complete backup but describes only “saved-copy/Archive references”; Entry 52 (client) says “JSON for a complete backup” without identifying that preserved HTML/PDF data itself is absent.
decision.note: At prototype review, the user-facing backup omitted actual saved-copy payloads, but the response did not surface that difference. It was detected later during implementation review.

decision.evidence: Entry 56 (client) asks to verify complete JSON restoration; Entry 57 (maker) claims saved HTML/PDF content round-trips; Entry 58 (client) reports the downloadable file contains only metadata and cannot restore the copy independently.
decision.note: This is one linked implementation-review decision: the initial verification request remained pending until the client tested the claimed fix and rejected the actual metadata-only export.

decision.evidence: Entry 59 (maker) verifies the exact UI export→fresh-account import→open flow with embedded HTML/PDF data; Entry 60 (client): “the corrected export now includes the preserved content itself.”
decision.note: The corrected user-facing backup and independent restore conform, and the client accepts the cycle.
